strategy_objective_guidance:
- The supplied evaluator code contains only a lock wrapper and calls an unavailable `evaluator.py`; no `combined_score`, test instances, validity checks, or numerical score weights are shown. Therefore the evaluator-visible scored terms and their weights cannot be decomposed from the provided material.
- The only stated nominal objective is to minimize the maximum per-GPU KVPR:
  \[
  \max_g \frac{\sum_{m\in g}(\mathrm{req\_rate}_m/\mathrm{slo}_m)}
                   {\mathrm{GPU\_MEM\_SIZE}-\sum_{m\in g}\mathrm{model\_size}_m}.
  \]
  The stated hard constraint is that every assigned GPU must have positive remaining memory: \(\sum \mathrm{model\_size}<\mathrm{GPU\_MEM\_SIZE}\). Empty GPUs have KVPR zero.
- No evidence is provided that simplicity, runtime, balance of model counts, placement stability, or total utilization is rewarded. Do not optimize those unless the hidden `evaluator.py` confirms them. Likewise, no numerical claim can be made about terms being near maximum, far from maximum, conflicting, or about a largest remaining scoring lever.
- The displayed wrapper does not show `compute_model_placement`’s signature or call pattern, so complete-input availability is not provable from the supplied evaluator. If the function receives the complete model list and GPU list—as model-placement functions normally do—it permits an offline/batch global assignment solver; do not restrict the design to causal greedy placement. If it is called incrementally, retain a fast forward greedy fallback.
- For the nominal minimax-KVPR objective, memory use and request-pressure load conflict: assigning a high-pressure model to a GPU raises its numerator, while assigning a large model reduces its denominator. A placement that merely balances request pressure or merely balances memory can be poor on the actual ratio objective.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
EXAMPLES OF DIFFERENT approaches:
- [Global threshold-feasibility MILP] Binary-search a candidate maximum KVPR \(t\); for each GPU enforce \(\sum_m[(req\_rate_m/slo_m)+t\,model\_size_m]x_{mg}\le t\,GPU\_MEM\_SIZE\), plus one-GPU-per-model and strict-memory-safe capacity constraints. This directly targets the nominal maximum ratio globally; `scipy.optimize: milp, LinearConstraint, Bounds` uses the available HiGHS MILP backend.
- [Batch nonlinear local optimization] Optimize a continuous assignment relaxation or directly polish a discrete placement against the maximum KVPR, then round and repair capacity violations; `scipy.optimize: differential_evolution, shgo, minimize` can explore non-greedy placements, but must return integral feasible assignments.
- [Deterministic ratio-aware greedy] Sort models by difficulty, such as large model size combined with high `req_rate/slo`, and place each onto the feasible GPU producing the smallest resulting maximum KVPR. This preserves the memory constraint and supplies a low-overhead fallback if MILP runtime is evaluator-limited.
- [Greedy plus exchange neighborhood search] Start with a feasible placement, then repeatedly apply improving one-model moves, pairwise GPU swaps, and small ejection chains whenever they lower the global maximum KVPR while retaining positive residual memory. `numpy: argsort, argmin` supports fast recomputation; this improves the evaluator-visible peak rather than cosmetic balance.
- [Stochastic discrete search] Use simulated annealing or randomized restarts over feasible relocations/swaps, retaining only assignments with positive residual memory. This complements deterministic greedy methods when multiple tightly packed GPUs create local minima; `numpy.random: default_rng` provides reproducible seeded proposals.
strategy_refine_guidance:
EXAMPLES OF REFINEMENT approaches:
- MILP bisection; initialize the lower bound with the best possible aggregate-pressure/aggregate-free-memory bound and the upper bound from a feasible greedy placement; use `scipy.optimize.milp` feasibility at each threshold.
- Strict capacity handling; reserve a small numerical memory epsilon so every returned GPU has `used_model_memory <= GPU_MEM_SIZE - epsilon`, preventing division by zero or evaluator rejection from floating-point equality.
- MILP time budget; set `scipy.optimize.milp` option `time_limit` and retain the best known feasible greedy assignment if a proof of threshold infeasibility cannot be obtained in time.
- Candidate-threshold tolerance; stop bisection only when the KVPR interval is below a scale-aware tolerance, then run a final exact feasibility check at the selected upper bound.
- Greedy ordering; test descending `model_size`, descending `req_rate/slo`, and descending normalized difficulty such as `(req_rate/slo)/(GPU_MEM_SIZE-model_size)`; keep the ordering with the lowest final maximum KVPR.
- Local-search focus; prioritize moves involving the current worst-KVPR GPU and accept a move only if it lowers the lexicographically sorted vector of GPU KVPRs, avoiding changes that improve a non-peak GPU while worsening the evaluated maximum.
- Repair initialization; after any rounded or randomized assignment, move models from over-capacity GPUs using the placement with minimum resulting peak KVPR; reject if no strictly memory-feasible destination exists.

strategies.title: [threshold-milp] Global KVPR threshold feasibility search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: threshold-milp  
Replacement scope: Replace the initial greedy-placement block and both subsequent local-search loops inside `compute_model_placement` with a global binary search over KVPR thresholds, using a binary MILP feasibility solve at each threshold.  
Compute budget: At most 12 MILP threshold solves; each solve has a hard `time_limit` of 0.15 seconds, and skip MILP entirely when `gpu_num * len(models) > 180`; expected evaluation-time effect is a bounded increase for small and medium instances, with the existing greedy/local-search construction retained as fallback.  
Gain mechanism: For a fixed candidate maximum pressure `t`, each GPU has the linear constraint `sum((weight + t * size) * x) <= t * GPU_MEM_SIZE`, so feasibility exactly represents whether a placement can achieve maximum KVPR at most `t`. This changes the search from local relocation/swap improvement into a global assignment construction that can simultaneously move arbitrarily many models among GPUs. Enforce one assignment per model, model-memory usage at most `GPU_MEM_SIZE - 1e-9`, and validate the returned integral assignment before accepting it; otherwise retain the feasible incumbent placement. Expected-gain check: this adds globally coordinated multi-model reassignment choices that the incumbent's strictly improving one-move and one-for-one-swap neighborhoods cannot realize, and it passes the falsifiable evaluator threshold if reported raw `max_kvpr` is below `24.7964708423`.

strategies.title: [ejection-chain] Two-for-one exchange neighborhood
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ejection-chain  
Replacement scope: Replace the existing pairwise-swap loop with a best-improvement variable-neighborhood loop containing relocations, one-for-one swaps, and directed two-model-for-one-model exchanges between every ordered pair of GPUs.  
Compute budget: No optimizer starts; at most 40 accepted neighborhood improvements, with exhaustive two-for-one candidate evaluation per pass; expected evaluation-time effect is moderate and proportional to the cube of the largest GPU model-list size.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent cannot leave a local optimum when reducing the worst GPU requires removing two moderately sized or high-pressure models while returning one large low-pressure model to maintain capacity. For each ordered source/target GPU pair, exchange every source-model pair against every target model, require both resulting residual capacities to remain at least `1e-9`, and accept only the candidate minimizing the global maximum KVPR. Update placement, free memory, and pressure weight atomically after each accepted exchange. Expected-gain check: this explicitly permits a capacity-preserving three-model contact topology unavailable to the incumbent's one-model moves and pair swaps, and it passes the falsifiable evaluator threshold if reported raw `max_kvpr` is below `24.7964708423`.

strategies.title: [lexicographic-vnd] Interleaved lexicographic local refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: lexicographic-vnd  
Replacement scope: Replace the two separate “finish all relocations, then finish all swaps” loops with one bounded variable-neighborhood descent loop that reevaluates relocations and swaps after every accepted change.  
Compute budget: No optimizer starts; at most 60 accepted improvements; expected evaluation-time effect is small relative to the current exhaustive move and swap scans.  
Gain mechanism: The current phase ordering creates an avoidable local-search bottleneck: a swap can lower the peak but make a newly useful relocation possible, yet relocations are never reconsidered after swapping. Compare trial states by the descending sorted vector of all GPU KVPRs, not only its maximum, so equal-peak moves are accepted only when they strictly reduce the next bottleneck and preserve future descent opportunities. Every candidate must leave each GPU with at least `1e-9` GB remaining. Expected-gain check: this introduces swap-then-relocate trajectories structurally impossible in the incumbent's one-pass phase order, and it passes the falsifiable evaluator threshold if reported raw `max_kvpr` is below `24.7964708423`.

strategies.title: [three-cycle-vnd] Cyclic three-GPU local refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: three-cycle-vnd  
Replacement scope: Replace the existing `improve` local-search phase, including its relocation, one-for-one swap, and directed two-for-one exchange enumeration.  
Compute budget: At most 40 VND passes; in each pass inspect all relocations and swaps, then at most 20,000 deterministic cyclic three-GPU exchanges. Expected evaluation-time effect: modest increase only on instances with many models, bounded by the exchange cap.  
Gain mechanism: The incumbent can transfer load between only two GPUs at a time. A placement can require a simultaneous cycle `A -> B -> C -> A` because neither individual move nor either pairwise swap fits memory or improves the lexicographic pressure vector. For every ordered GPU triple, test one model from each GPU and rotate them cyclically; accept only a strict improvement in the sorted descending vector of GPU KVPRs. Maintain exact weight and remaining-memory arrays, and reject every candidate with any remaining memory below `EPS`.  
The implementation should retain the best incumbent placement, evaluate each feasible cycle using the exact post-cycle denominators, and apply the best lexicographically improving move before restarting the neighborhood scan. Expected-gain check: this adds feasible three-way reassignment edges that the incumbent’s two-GPU neighborhoods cannot represent; it passes the falsifiable threshold only if the evaluator reports `combined_score > 26.174758`.

strategies.title: [restricted-reoptimization] Exact worst-GPU subsystem replacement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: restricted-reoptimization  
Replacement scope: Replace the final single full-instance MILP polishing block with a restricted MILP repair phase applied after local search.  
Compute budget: At most 3 restricted solves per seed, each with one threshold MILP bisection of at most 8 feasibility calls and 0.10 seconds per call. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded increase, substantially smaller than solving the entire instance repeatedly.  
Gain mechanism: Freeze GPUs whose KVPR is safely below the current peak and jointly reoptimize a mesoscopic subsystem containing the current worst GPU, the next two highest-pressure GPUs, and one low-pressure buffer GPU. Models on those selected GPUs are reassigned only among that GPU subset, while the frozen GPUs remain unchanged. The MILP uses the exact threshold constraint `sum((value_i + t * size_i) * x_i,g) <= t * GPU_MEM_SIZE`, assignment equalities, and strict capacity `sum(size_i*x_i,g) <= GPU_MEM_SIZE-EPS`. This allows coordinated reassignment of many models among four GPUs, which pairwise and small ejection neighborhoods cannot make.  
Use the current placement peak as the initial upper bound, the aggregate-free-memory bound on the selected GPUs as the lower bound, and retain the candidate only after reconstructing and exactly checking every GPU’s remaining memory and KVPR. Expected-gain check: this can cross local-search barriers by replacing an entire four-GPU assignment while preserving all frozen assignments; it passes the falsifiable threshold only if the evaluator reports `combined_score > 26.174758`.

strategies.title: [pattern-set-partitioning] Enumerated feasible GPU-pattern master solve
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: pattern-set-partitioning  
Replacement scope: Replace the global threshold-MILP block for compact instances with a pattern-based set-partitioning threshold solve.  
Compute budget: Only when `n <= 22`; enumerate at most `2^n` subsets while discarding subsets whose memory is not strictly feasible, then perform at most 10 master feasibility solves with a 0.15-second limit each. Expected evaluation-time effect: none for larger instances and bounded compact-instance overhead.  
Gain mechanism: Instead of assigning one model-GPU edge at a time, represent every strictly memory-feasible subset of models as a complete GPU configuration with its exact memory and pressure contribution. At a target KVPR threshold, retain only configurations satisfying `subset_value <= t * (GPU_MEM_SIZE-subset_size)`, then solve a set-partitioning master problem selecting exactly `gpu_num` configurations whose model-incidence vectors cover every model exactly once. This configuration representation directly captures dense multi-model packing structures that assignment-variable relaxation and local exchanges can miss.  
Discard empty duplicate configurations except as needed to fill unused GPUs, require every selected configuration to have positive residual memory, reconstruct the placement from selected patterns, and preserve the existing placement as fallback if enumeration or the master solve is incomplete. Expected-gain check: the master can choose globally compatible whole-GPU packings unavailable as any sequence of incumbent local moves; it passes the falsifiable threshold only if the evaluator reports `combined_score > 26.174758`.

strategies.title: [global-threshold-milp] Direct assignment threshold feasibility search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: global-threshold-milp  
Replacement scope: Replace the `if n and n <= 22:` enumerated-pattern set-partitioning block with a direct model-to-GPU binary assignment MILP threshold search that operates on all model counts supported by the solver-size guard.  
Compute budget: At most 7 MILP feasibility solves per placement call, each with a 0.12-second HiGHS limit; skip the MILP when `n * gpu_num > 320`; expected evaluation-time increase is bounded by about 0.84 seconds only on solver-eligible instances and is normally substantially lower because feasibility models terminate quickly.  
Gain mechanism: For a threshold \(t\), assign every model directly with the linear per-GPU constraint \(\sum_i (v_i+t s_i)x_{ig}\le80t\), plus strict memory capacity. Unlike complete-pattern enumeration, this can optimize globally without enumerating \(2^n\) subsets and is not restricted to `n <= 22`; unlike greedy/VND, it can simultaneously alter every GPU assignment to cross disconnected packing basins. Build the incumbent greedy/VND solution first, use its peak as the feasible upper bound, use total pressure divided by total free memory as the lower bound, and retain only fully integral, independently memory-validated solver assignments.  
Expected-gain check: the incumbent cannot represent a globally coordinated reassignment unless it happens to be reachable through its bounded local moves or its `n <= 22` pattern enumeration, whereas this construction tests such assignments directly; the falsifiable acceptance threshold is `combined_score > 26.255972` with all returned GPU residual memories strictly positive.

strategies.title: [two-two-exchange] Exact paired block exchange around peak GPUs
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: paired-block-exchange  
Replacement scope: Replace the current pairwise single-model swap loop inside `improve` with a staged neighborhood containing ordinary swaps followed by exact two-model-for-two-model exchanges between the current worst GPU and every other GPU.  
Compute budget: At most 30 accepted refinement iterations; on each iteration inspect at most the two highest-pressure source GPUs, at most 12 highest-difficulty models from each source and destination GPU, and at most 10,000 candidate block exchanges; expected evaluation-time increase is modest and bounded by the candidate cap.  
Gain mechanism: A one-model swap cannot move a pressure-heavy small model together with a compensating large low-pressure model, because either intermediate one-model move may violate memory or worsen the peak. Enumerate source pairs `{i,j}` and destination pairs `{k,l}`, calculate the two changed numerators and residual memories exactly, and accept only a strict improvement of the sorted pressure vector. The simultaneous four-model contact changes both numerator balance and denominator balance while maintaining feasibility at the only states that matter. Models outside the capped difficulty lists remain available to ordinary moves and swaps.  
Expected-gain check: the incumbent’s move, one-for-one swap, and three-GPU one-item cycle neighborhoods cannot realize a simultaneous two-for-two transfer, so this adds a strictly new feasible transition; the falsifiable acceptance threshold is `combined_score > 26.255972` while every tested and returned exchange satisfies residual memory `>= EPS`.

strategies.title: [worst-bin-ruin-repair] Deterministic pressure-aware ruin-and-repair neighborhoo
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: adaptive-large-neighborhood  
Replacement scope: Add a bounded restart phase after the best greedy/VND seed and before any global solver phase; it replaces neither the incumbent fallback nor the final local polishing pass.  
Compute budget: Exactly 6 deterministic ruin-repair starts, each removing at most 8 models and followed by at most 20 move/swap polishing iterations; expected evaluation-time effect is linear in the removed-model count and substantially below exhaustive subset enumeration.  
Gain mechanism: Form six distinct destroy sets from the highest-pressure GPUs: largest models, largest pressure values, largest `value/(80-size)` difficulty, and mixed pairs from the two worst GPUs. Remove the selected models, leaving all other assignments fixed, then reinsert removed models in descending difficulty by selecting the feasible destination minimizing the resulting lexicographic pressure signature. Finish with normal VND. This permits several models to leave a congested GPU before any replacement is inserted, escaping capacity barriers that prevent one-step relocations and swaps without requiring a full restricted exact reoptimization. Every partial repair checks strict positive remaining memory before insertion.  
Expected-gain check: the incumbent local search only evaluates changes from a complete feasible placement and therefore cannot traverse a sequence whose beneficial rearrangement requires temporarily unassigning several models, while this bounded destroy-set topology can; the falsifiable acceptance threshold is `combined_score > 26.255972` with no unassigned models and positive residual memory on every GPU.

strategies.title: [ejection-chain] Peak-GPU two-for-one ejection refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ejection-chain  
Replacement scope: Replace the current `improve(place, rem, weight, limit=40)` function with a peak-focused lexicographic neighborhood that retains one-model moves and swaps but adds exact one-for-two exchanges between two GPUs.  
Compute budget: At most 35 improvement rounds; at most 30,000 evaluated one-for-two exchanges per round, prioritizing exchanges involving a currently maximum-pressure GPU. Expected evaluation-time effect: modest increase over the current VND, bounded independently of the number of possible cubic exchanges.  
Gain mechanism: The current implementation can exchange only one model for one model or rotate three singleton models. It cannot remove a difficult large/high-pressure model from a saturated peak GPU while returning two smaller models whose combined memory and pressure composition fit better. For each ordered GPU pair `(a, b)`, test replacing model `i` on `a` by every feasible unordered pair `(j, k)` on `b`, update only those two GPU pressure ratios, and choose the lexicographically best sorted pressure vector. Apply only strict improvements. This changes both the numerator and residual-memory denominator on the bottleneck GPU in a way unavailable to singleton moves, swaps, or singleton cycles. strategies.title: [tabu-plateau-search] Deterministic tabu escape from strict lexicographic local
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-plateau-search  
Replacement scope: Replace the existing `improve(place, rem, weight, limit=40)` phase entirely.  
Compute budget: At most 3 deterministic starts from the best greedy/beam placements; at most 120 accepted transitions per start; inspect at most 250 move/swap candidates per transition; expected evaluation-time effect is a small bounded increase.  
Gain mechanism: The current refinement accepts only lexicographically improving moves, swaps, and cycles, so it cannot cross a feasible plateau or a temporary worsening required to free memory on a nearly full GPU. Use a deterministic tabu search over feasible one-model moves and swaps: rank candidates by resulting peak KVPR first and sorted KVPR vector second; permit a non-improving transition when no improving transition exists; forbid reversing the same item movement for 7 transitions unless it improves the globally best placement; retain the best feasible placement ever seen. Generate candidates preferentially from the current peak GPU and its two closest-pressure destination GPUs, then fill the bounded candidate pool with deterministic global candidates. Every candidate must preserve `remaining[g] > EPS`; update placement only after checking both affected GPUs. Return the globally best placement, never the final plateau state.  
Expected-gain check: this introduces feasible plateau-crossing item trajectories that the incumbent’s strictly improving VND cannot realize, and it is falsified unless the evaluator reports `combined_score > 26.2559717495` while retaining success rate 1.

strategies.title: [beam-packing-construction] Bounded multi-hypothesis ratio-aware construction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-packing-construction  
Replacement scope: Replace the `orders` loop and its single-path `build(order)` calls with a bounded beam constructor, keeping subsequent refinement unchanged.  
Compute budget: One deterministic beam search of width 24 for `n <= 35` and `gpu_num <= 12`; otherwise use the existing best greedy construction; no optimizer starts; expected evaluation-time effect is bounded by roughly `24 * n * gpu_num` placement expansions plus sorting.  
Gain mechanism: Each existing greedy order commits irrevocably to one GPU for every early model. Instead, process models in descending difficulty `(value / max(EPS, 80-size), size, value)`, retain up to 24 distinct partial assignments after every model, and branch each retained state once for each distinct feasible GPU state. Score a partial state by the sorted vector of current pressures followed by total used memory on the most crowded GPUs; canonicalize equivalent GPUs by sorting `(weight, remaining)` only for beam deduplication, while retaining concrete assignments. This preserves competing early packing topologies, particularly whether a large low-request model should reserve capacity for a later high-pressure model. Discard only states with nonpositive residual memory. Feed the best complete beam states through the existing local refinement and keep the best peak.  
Expected-gain check: the beam can retain mutually incompatible early placements that no single incumbent greedy path can revisit after committing its first conflicting assignment, and it is falsified unless the evaluator reports `combined_score > 26.2559717495`.

strategies.title: [symmetry-bnb-threshold] Symmetry-reduced exact threshold branch-and-bound
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: symmetry-bnb-threshold  
Replacement scope: Replace the `if n and n <= 22:` pattern-enumeration/set-partitioning MILP block with a bounded symmetry-reduced threshold feasibility search for small instances.  
Compute budget: For `n <= 16`, perform at most 20 threshold probes and at most 250,000 recursive nodes per probe; for larger instances skip this phase; expected evaluation-time effect is bounded and small on instances where the exact search is enabled.  
Gain mechanism: For a candidate pressure threshold `t`, each model has threshold consumption `value[i] + t * size[i]`, and each GPU has budget `t * GPU_MEM_SIZE`; a feasible bin additionally has strictly positive residual memory. Recursively assign models ordered by descending threshold consumption, trying only one representative among GPUs with identical `(used_threshold_consumption, used_size)` states. Prune using total remaining threshold capacity, direct per-model fit, and canonical-bin symmetry. A feasible leaf is a global certificate for that threshold and supplies an assignment; binary search between the aggregate lower bound and the incumbent feasible peak. Unlike the incumbent’s pattern MILP, this directly exploits indistinguishable-GPU symmetry during search and can complete exact threshold feasibility without constructing every feasible subset or relying on a short external solver time limit.  
Expected-gain check: whenever it finds a feasible threshold strictly below the incumbent peak, that assignment has a strictly lower nominal maximum KVPR than the incumbent, and the strategy is falsified unless such cases raise evaluator `combined_score` above `26.2559717495`.
